blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Accounting is the language of Czarnikow's numbers. Today's topic is Accounts Payable. These are short, simple sentences you can use with the finance team.

You will learn five useful words: supplier, payable, please, confirm, and amount. Practise them in short, natural sentences. Take it slow — one step at a time.

💛 A small tip: English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts. You can do it!

items.q: What is today's topic?
items.why: "Today's topic is Accounts Payable."

items.q: How many new words will you learn?
items.why: "You will learn five useful words."

items.q: Who can you use these sentences with?
items.why: "sentences you can use with the finance team."

items.q: The text says "take it slow." This suggests that…
items.why: Inferência: "take it slow — one step at a time" quer dizer sem pressa.

items.q: The tip "English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts" suggests the author wants you to feel…
items.why: Inferência: "You can do it!" é uma mensagem de confiança.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentar o tema para um novo estagiário. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hello! Welcome to the accounting team. My name is Sophie. Today we start with Accounts Payable. Don't worry — it is easy. We use short and simple words.

A supplier is a company that sells things to us. When we get a bill, we have money to pay. This money is called a payable. We check the amount, and then we pay.

Here is a polite way to ask for help. You can say: "Could you confirm the amount, please?" Or: "Would you send me the file, please?" The word please is very important. It is kind and professional.

Let's practise together. Say it with me: "Please confirm the amount." Very good! One more time: "Could you check the supplier, please?" Nice work.

Take it slow. One step at a time. You can do it!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the topic of Sophie's lesson today?
items.why: "Today we start with Accounts Payable."

items.q: What is a supplier, according to Sophie?
options: A company that sells things to us
A person on the finance team
items.why: "A supplier is a company that sells things to us."

items.q: Which polite question does Sophie give as an example?
options: Could you confirm the amount, please?
items.why: "Could you confirm the amount, please?"

items.q: Why does Sophie say "the word please is very important"?
options: Because it is a long word
Because it sounds kind and professional
Because it is hard to say
items.why: Inferência: ela diz que é "kind and professional".

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone with the new trainee?
items.why: Inferência: "Don't worry", "Very good!", "You can do it!" mostram apoio.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our new supplier sends the coffee every week." A supplier is…
options: a company that sells to us
items.why: Supplier = fornecedor, quem vende para nós.

items.q: "We have one payable to check today." A payable is money that…
items.why: Payable = a pagar, dinheiro que devemos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please ___ the number before you send it."
items.why: Confirm = confirmar; encaixa como verbo na frase.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ on this bill is 500 dollars."
items.why: Amount = valor, a quantia na conta.

items.q: "Can you help me, please?" We use please to…
items.why: Please = por favor, deixa o pedido educado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e pedidos educados que aparecem no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Could you send the file?" We use "could you" to…
items.why: "Could you…?" é um pedido educado.

items.q: "Would you confirm the amount, please?" This is…
items.why: "Would you…, please?" também é um pedido educado.

items.q: The manager will sign off on the payment. This means she will…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval.

items.q: "Can you follow up with the supplier?" To follow up means to…
items.why: Follow up = dar sequência, checar de novo depois.

items.q: "Let's go over the numbers together." To go over means to…
items.why: Go over = revisar, olhar com atenção.
